newsitem.title: USA: Cold hits Kansas, Nebraska HRW wheat areas.
newsitem.headline: Cold hits Kansas, Nebraska HRW wheat areas.

text.p: Sub-freezing temperatures blanketed the hard red winter wheat areas of northwest Kansas and southwest Nebraska early Friday morning, but meteorologists said the wheat probably was not damaged.
"It was close to being cold enough to cause some damage," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.

Lows dipped to 23 degrees Fahrenheit in Sidney in the southern Nebraska Panhandle. Karen DeBoer, an agriculture extension agent for Cheyenne County, Neb., said it was too early to determine if the cold hurt the wheat, which was just past the jointing stage.
Goodland in northwest Kansas had a record low of 29 degrees, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, but he doubted the wheat was mature enough to be hurt.
Wheat in northwest Kansas needs rain, but neither Burgio nor Solberg expect much moisture there through next week. Scattered showers were likely Tuesday in the eastern hard red winter wheat areas.
"The area that needs it is northwest Kansas and there's not much there at all," said Burgio.
